messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Streaming route /v1/stream is breaching p99 latency SLO. Paging on-call. Detected spike at 6123456789.
incident-bot: Metrics snapshot: p95=900ms -> 1.1s, p99=450ms -> 3.2s, error rate 504s up 0.7%. Affected region: eu-west-1.

oncall-alex: Acked. I'm on it. Paging eng-runtime + eng-platform. Can someone grab customer impact? :eyes:

sre-maya: I'll pull logs and traces now. Preliminary note: spike correlates with sustained KEEPALIVE reset rates on proxy nodes and increased client-side stalled writes.

engineer-jordan: seeing a lot of long tail writes in the proxy logs. sample: 
```
[proxy-12] 2026-03-15T12:34:55Z upstream read timeout (30s) "upstream timed out while reading response header from upstream" route=/v1/stream
[stream] client_backpressure=true stalled_chunks=74 socket_write_ms=25000
```

eng-runtime: Looks like streaming chunk flushes are being held by the backend because of KV cache thrash and a spike in large-seq requests. Queue depth on runtime workers jumped from 12 -> 140 on some hosts.

eng-platform: Proxy pool CPU and epoll backlog also increased; we see socket buffer saturation and many connections hitting 30s upstream timeout. ALB logs show increased processing time but not 5xx at ALB level.

support-lee: Customer impact: several enterprise customers reported perceived stall (clients show long pauses between initial chunk and subsequent chunks). Tickets opened: 6 customers, 3 P1s, intermittent.

product-sam: TL;DR: streaming clients get initial data then stalled ~10-30s. Mobile clients more affected due to smaller recv windows. Need mitigation plan.

oncall-alex: Immediate mitigations we can try: 1) enable short circuit fallback (streaming->non-streaming) via admin flag for affected customers, 2) scale up runtime workers for /v1/stream, 3) temporarily increase proxy keepalive and lower chunk buffer sizes. Which can we do quickly?

eng-platform: I can scale proxy pool + route traffic to warm hosts. Increasing keepalive timeout is risky but doable on a rolling basis. Recommend scaling runtime first. I'll open a scaling job.

eng-runtime: I can increase worker count and reduce per-worker batch size. Pushing a config: 
```
api: /v1/stream
workers: 2 -> 8
batch_size: 32 -> 8
kv_cache_ttl: 600 -> 120 (for hot reload)
```
I'll deploy to canary groups in eu-west-1 now.

engineer-jordan: Also toggling a temporary server-side throttle to drop very large seq requests (len>2048) — they cause head-of-line blocking for many shorter requests.

support-lee: Noting which customers to target for flag: cust-foo, cust-bar, cust-baz (all complaining). If we flip fallback for them we can reduce perceived outages.

oncall-alex: Do it. Provide the admin command.

eng-platform: Admin API (internal) command to flip fallback for a customer:
```
curl -XPOST "https://admin.internal/flags" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"customer_id":"cust-foo","flag":"streaming.force_no_stream","value":true}'
```
Note: this will route their requests to non-streaming generator until we clear the issue.

engineer-jordan: Pushed small sample change: drop requests where chunk_count>64 or seq_len>2048. Rolling out to 10% now. Watch for error rates.

incident-bot: NOTE: page routed to eng-runtime, eng-platform, oncall-alex.

sre-maya: Traces show that when a backend worker hits large GC/serialization pauses, the connection remains open but backpressure prevents flushing for other clients sharing the same proxy connection. It's a mixture of client backpressure + worker-level head-of-line blocking.

eng-runtime: Confirmed: worker logs show a pattern: expensive evals (long seq) cause KV cache misses -> model layers stall -> socket buffer fills -> proxy stalls other streams multiplexed on same worker.

engineer-jordan: Quick diagnostic curl to test streaming flush behavior (run from eu-west):
```
curl -v --no-buffer -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream" -d '{"prompt":"small"}'
```
If response pauses after chunk1 reproduce.

oncall-alex: After scaling and canary, we need to monitor p95/p99 and client complaints. Target: p99 < 1s within 15m or escalate to incident commander.

eng-platform: Scaling job started: scaled runtime pool by +3 hosts, spun up extra proxy nodes. Rolling canary to 10% traffic in 2 min.

sre-maya: After canary we see p99 drop from 3.2s -> 1.4s on canary hosts. Overall traffic still high, but trend good.

product-sam: Noted: user-visible improvement on canary. Suggest we continue scale and then gradually reduce aggressive throttles once stable.

support-lee: Contacted top 3 complaining customers with update and mitigation steps (flipping fallback). They asked for ETA. I told them 15-30m for mitigation to finish.

eng-runtime: Rolling updates applied to 50% of servers. Observed worker queue depth normalizing. However one host shows repeated GC spikes and delayed socket writes. Marking host runtime-17 for drain and reprovision.

engineer-jordan: Quick patch: reduce long-request window by rejecting requests with tokens>4096 at admission with a 429 and instruct clients to use chunked smaller prompts. This will be reverted once KV/cache config tuned.

oncall-alex: Good. Summarize mitigation steps for handoff: 1) scaled runtime + proxies, 2) disabled streaming for affected customers via admin flag, 3) temporary request-size rejection for extremes, 4) drained problematic runtime hosts, 5) collecting postmortem artifacts.

incident-bot: HANDOFF: oncall-alex is handing off to eng-runtime for follow-through and postmortem.

oncall-alex: Handoff notes for next shift:
- Root cause hypothesis: head-of-line blocking from large-seq requests causing worker stalls -> proxy socket buffer saturation -> upstream timeouts causing streaming chunk stalls.
- Key metrics: p95 before=120ms now ~900ms; p99 peaked 3.2s; proxy 504s increased 0.7%.
- Actions taken: scaled runtime, scaled proxies, flipped fallback for 3 customers, drained repro host runtime-17, applied request-size admission control.
- Followups: investigate KV cache eviction policy, add per-client streaming queueing isolation, add circuit-breaker for long-eval requests, adjust batch sizing heuristics.

eng-runtime: I'll own the postmortem. I'll collect: perf traces for runtime-17, full proxy logs for the 15m window, and the change list. Will open PM with timeline + RCA. ETA for initial RCA draft: 48h.

support-lee: I'll keep customers updated and collect any additional reproductions.

product-sam: Add a prompt-level eval to detect large-seq jobs that should be routed to non-streaming path automatically.

oncall-alex: Thanks team. I'll close the immediate page since mitigation is active and p99 trending down. If p99 crosses threshold again, re-open page. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: Mitigated -> monitoring.

sre-maya: Post-incident ask: add a dashboard for "streaming chunk inter-arrival time" and per-proxy socket write latency to catch this earlier.

engineer-jordan: +1 to that. Also add an internal alert for sustained queue depth > 50 on runtime hosts.

eng-platform: Noted. Will add alerts and followups to the backlog.

support-lee: Closing customer loop: all flagged customers were notified; three accepted the fallback; two asked for postmortem.

oncall-alex: Closing thread. Thanks all for quick responses.
